title: Back into Plato's Cave: Examining Cross-modal Representational Convergence at Scale
abstract: arXiv:2604.18572v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis posits that neural networks trained on different modalities (e.g., text and images) converge toward a shared representation of reality. If true, this has significant implications for whether modality choice matters at all. In this paper, we show that the evidence for this claim is substantially weaker than subsequent work suggests. The mutual $k$-nearest-neighbor metric used on 1024 text-image pairs in the original study captures only coarse structure. To keep the alignment from collapsing as one scales up the data, $k$ has to grow proportionally, undercutting the argument for fine-grained representational convergence. The reported increase in alignment with language model strength saturates for recent models. translated_title: 回到柏拉图的洞穴：大规模检验跨模态表征趋同性
translated_abstract: 柏拉图表征假说认为，在不同模态（如文本和图像）上训练的神经网络会收敛到对现实的共享表征。如果这一假说成立，将对模态选择是否重要这一问题产生重大影响。本文表明，支持这一论断的证据远比后续研究所暗示的弱得多。原始研究中在1024个文本-图像对上使用的互k近邻度量只能捕捉粗粒度结构。为了在数据规模扩大时防止对齐度崩溃，k必须按比例增长，这削弱了细粒度表征趋同的论证。所报告的与语言模型能力相关的对齐度提升在近期模型中已经饱和。此外，一对一的文本-图像配对有利于对齐，而在非双射数据下对齐度会降低。我们进一步发现，图像和文本表征确实共享粗粒度……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文重新检验了柏拉图表征假说，发现其证据远比此前认为的弱——原始度量只能捕捉粗粒度结构、对齐度提升在近期模型中已饱和、且高度依赖一对一数据配对，从而削弱了细粒度跨模态表征趋同的论证。
en_tdlr: This paper re-examines the Platonic Representation Hypothesis and shows its evidence is substantially weaker than previously suggested—the original metric captures only coarse structure, alignment gains saturate for recent models, and alignment depends on one-to-one data pairing—undercutting claims of fine-grained cross-modal representational convergence.
